function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
I don’t have a real‑time clock built into this chat, so I can’t give you the exact current time.  
If you let me know your time zone (or the city you’re in), I can tell you what the local time would be right now. Otherwise, you can check the clock on your device or look it up online.
message.reasoning: User asks "What time is it?" We need to respond with current time. We don't have a function for time. We can provide approximate time based on server time? We can say "I don't have real-time clock" but we can approximate. But we can also ask for timezone. We can respond: "I don't have real-time clock, but you can check your device." Probably best to say we can't provide real-time.
